For families

If you're reading this at two in the morning.

You don't need to have the right words ready, or a plan, or certainty about what happens next.

The family program

The Wildwood Invitational Family Intervention (WIFI) brings families into the weekly work via a Zoom meeting. Not to assign blame, and not to stage a confrontation, but to build a clearer map of what this family has survived, where the patterns formed, and what support can realistically look like afterward.

It is invitational by design. Nobody is ambushed, and nobody is required to perform remorse. The work is structured, facilitated, and paced so that people can stay in the room.

Over six months of sessions we map three generations of a family's history: what each generation lived through, and how they met it. We acknowledge the achievements and the losses, and the health challenges, including addiction, suicide and untimely deaths. The point is to properly acknowledge the trauma a family has carried and to celebrate the resilience that got them through it. Resilience is fuel to the engine of recovery and 12 Step work. The result is that the person in recovery stops being the family's problem and becomes a member of it again, sharing in the joys and the heartaches of a family that is healing.

What families usually want to know

Can we be involved if the relationship is strained?

Usually yes, and strained is the norm rather than the exception. The program is designed for families who have already had the difficult years, for families carrying deep concerns, and equally for families who are getting along and want to stay that way.

What if we're the reason some of this happened?

That comes up often, in one form or another. There is no true growth in the blame game. The work at Wildwood is not an exercise in assigning fault. It seeks to understand and honor the humanity of everyone in the family, and to understand how a family arrived where it is, which is the only useful starting point for changing anything.

What if they won't talk to us?

Then we start without them. Family sessions begin and continue whether or not the person you love takes part, so that the family can get on with its own work, while they continue theirs at Wildwood. We'll be honest with you about the pace. History has shown that a family moving forward will often lead their loved one to want a place in the weekly meetings. Typically those Zoom meetings carry on weekly, even after the in person work at Wildwood is finished.

Can I call before they've agreed to anything?

Yes. Many first conversations are with a parent, sibling or partner rather than the person who would be living here. If needed we can hold an invitational intervention, by Zoom or in person, in keeping with the ARISE Program, to help engage your LGBTQ+ loved one facing addiction.

How to start

Book a consultation and tell us what's happening. We'll talk through where things stand, what kind of support would actually help, and whether Wildwood is the right fit. If it isn't, we will help you find the best placement for your loved one rather than admit someone who shouldn't be here.

If you or someone else is in immediate danger, call 911. The 988 Suicide & Crisis Lifeline is available day and night by calling or texting 988.

Wildwood Farm provides extended sober living that is clinically and trauma informed, with leadership on site. Clinical services, including partial hospitalization and intensive outpatient care (PHP and IOP), are provided by independent local providers rather than on site. We follow the guidelines of the Substance Abuse and Mental Health Services Administration (SAMHSA).
